Description: The map is divided into land territories and sea zones separated by borders.
Most territories have an IPC value that contributes to the controlling power's income; some have no income value.
The power whose emblem is printed on a territory is its original controller.
Territories are classified by control and political relationship; hostile means controlled by an enemy power at war.
Spaces are adjacent when they share a border; meeting only at a point does not establish adjacency.
The Sahara Desert and Pripet Marshes cannot be entered or crossed by units.
A sea zone is hostile when it contains enemy surface warships belonging to a power at war; submarines and transports alone do not make it hostile.
The Caspian Sea is treated as a sea zone despite having no zone number.
Each named island or island group is a territory; separate named islands in one sea zone can hold separate land units.
Unlabelled islands are not game spaces and cannot receive units.
Control of the land territories associated with a canal or strait determines whether sea units may pass through it.
Where multiple territories control a passage, the same side must control all of them; if opposing sides split control, the passage is closed.
A side may use a canal or strait only if it controlled the passage at the start of its turn; a passage captured during the turn cannot be used that turn.
Sea units cannot pass through a passage controlled by a neutral territory or a power at war with them.
Submarines may pass through the Strait of Gibraltar regardless of who controls it.
Canals and straits do not restrict air-unit movement.
At setup, France and the United Kingdom are at war with Germany and Italy; the United States and Soviet Union begin at peace.
Unless a political rule says otherwise, war is declared at the beginning of Combat Move, before any combat movement.
A declaration of war against one power does not automatically create war with every power on that side.
Declarations are classified as provoked when triggered by direct aggression or a specific political rule; other declarations are unprovoked.
Germany may declare war on the United States or Soviet Union at the beginning of Combat Move on any of its turns; these relationships are independent.

The Soviet Union cannot declare war on an Axis power before its fourth turn unless an Axis power declares war on it first; a captured London creates an additional permission on the Soviet following turn.
The United States is subject to the rulebook's specific timing and triggering conditions before entering the war.
Open Field / Issue: Use the exact national political trigger wording when implementing the rule.

Description: Neutral territories are divided into friendly neutrals, unfriendly neutrals and strict neutrals.
Friendly neutrals may be entered without combat; their control and subsequent movement are governed by the neutral rules.
A power not at war cannot move units into territories belonging to another friendly power or into friendly neutral territories during noncombat movement.
Entering an unfriendly neutral is a combat move, and its defending army must be eliminated before the invading power takes control.
Air units cannot fly over an unfriendly neutral unless they are attacking it.
An invaded neutral ceases to be neutral and joins the opposing side; its standing army is placed and managed for the battle by a power on that side.
Capturing an unfriendly neutral adds its territory income to the invading power's national production.
If an invasion fails, surviving neutral defenders remain in an uncontrolled territory, cannot move, and the territory becomes friendly to the side it joined.
Invading a strict neutral triggers the rulebook's strict-neutral consequences and defensive response.
Open Field / Issue: Keep the exact strict-neutral consequence wording in the player-facing rules.

Description: Power-specific political rules determine when otherwise friendly or neutral spaces may be entered.
Play proceeds in rounds; each power takes a turn in the fixed order printed in the rulebook.
A power's turn proceeds through Purchase and Repair, Combat Move, Conduct Combat, Noncombat Move, Mobilize New Units and Collect Income.
All phases except collecting income are voluntary, subject to the applicable rules.
Each power tracks a treasury of IPCs used to purchase units and pay applicable costs.
Each power begins with the income and treasury specified by the setup information.
A power's national production level is based on the combined IPC values of the territories it controls.
During Purchase and Repair, a power may buy units it can afford and later mobilize, subject to special purchasing restrictions.
A power is not required to spend its entire treasury during a purchase phase.
The number of units in play is not limited by the number of supplied plastic pieces; substitutes may represent additional units.
A power may pay IPCs to remove damage from eligible facilities; each damage point repaired costs 1 IPC.
Facility repairs take effect immediately, allowing the repaired facility to be used during the remainder of that turn.

Rule: Repair capital ships at naval bases
Description: Eligible damaged battleships and carriers in sea zones serviced by operative friendly naval bases are repaired during Purchase and Repair at no IPC cost.
Purchased units are first placed in the mobilization zone and are not usable until mobilized later in the turn.
Purchases are constrained by the power's ability to mobilize units during the current turn, after relevant facility repairs.
A power collects income from territories it controls during Collect Income, including income from territories captured during its turn.
When control of a territory changes, the relevant national production level is adjusted by that territory's IPC value.
Combat Move sends units into hostile spaces or performs other movement explicitly allowed during that phase.
Combat movement generally must end in a hostile space, except for specified special movements and setup actions.
Units that participate in combat movement generally cannot make another move in Noncombat Move.
Noncombat Move moves eligible units that did not participate in combat, subject to movement and location restrictions.
Land units may move into friendly or friendly-neutral territories, including territories captured earlier in the turn, but not hostile, unfriendly-neutral or strict-neutral territories.
An air unit's movement across the complete turn cannot exceed its move value, including reaching a legal landing place.
Air units must finish movement in a legal landing space within their movement allowance, subject to the carrier landing exception.
Air units attacking during Combat Move must generally reserve enough movement to reach a safe landing location during Noncombat Move.
Fighters and tactical bombers may use their full movement to attack a sea zone if a carrier can be present for them to land on by the end of Mobilize New Units.
Sea units normally move up to two sea zones; units departing a sea zone serviced by an operative friendly naval base may move up to three.
Sea units cannot move through hostile sea zones; they normally stop and enter combat when an enemy surface warship makes a zone hostile.
Submarines may pass through hostile sea zones without stopping unless an enemy destroyer is present.

Rule: Sea units in hostile starting zones
Description: Sea units that begin in a hostile zone choose among the movement and combat options specified by the Combat Move rules; after participating, they cannot move again during Noncombat Move.
Transports load land units in eligible friendly sea zones; loading and unloading are constrained by transport movement and amphibious-assault rules.
A transport carries land units up to its capacity as defined in its unit profile; land-unit combinations follow the transport rules.
Transported land units may unload according to the rules for ordinary movement or amphibious assault; unloading ends the transported unit's movement.
The attacker must announce intended amphibious assaults during Combat Move.
Land units, transports and supporting naval units follow the special movement and combat procedures for amphibious assaults.
Eligible tanks and mechanized infantry may move through an unoccupied hostile territory during a qualifying movement, subject to the blitz rules.
Artillery may support eligible infantry-type units to improve their attack, subject to pairing restrictions.
Movement through or into another power's territory is subject to alliance, war-status and phase-specific restrictions.
Naval movement through controlled canals and narrow straits follows the control, timing and exception rules in the map section.
Each contested territory or sea zone is resolved separately and completely; the attacker chooses the order of battles.
Attacking and defending units are considered to fire simultaneously, although dice are rolled attacker first for convenience.
Once a battle has begun, no new units may enter it as reinforcements.
Combat follows the seven-step general sequence: position units, submarine special step, attacker fire, defender fire, casualty removal, press or retreat, conclude.
A unit scores a hit when its attack or defence die roll is at or below its applicable combat value.
The player taking casualties selects eligible units according to the combat and special-unit rules; casualties are removed at the specified step.

Rule: Facilities do not fight in general combat
Description: Facilities do not participate in general combat; they are attacked and damaged through strategic or tactical bombing raids.
When hostile territory contains no combat units or contains only facilities and/or AAA, no general combat is required, though AAA may fire at attacking aircraft.
The attacker may retreat at the designated point in the combat sequence, following the retreat rules for the type of battle.
Combat continues through successive rounds until the battle is concluded by elimination, retreat or a special rule.
Submarines may make a surprise-strike roll before general sea combat when no opposing destroyer prevents it.
A submarine may submerge during the special submarine step, removing itself from the remaining battle sequence; opposing destroyers prevent this option.
Submarine surprise-strike hits target sea units, not air units; transports are eligible only when no other eligible sea units remain.
A destroyer suppresses submarine surprise strike and submergence and prevents submarines from passing through hostile sea zones under the relevant rules.
Battleships and carriers require two hits to be destroyed; one hit marks an undamaged capital ship as damaged.
A damaged battleship or carrier that survives combat may be repaired at an operative friendly naval base.
Battleships and cruisers may bombard during an amphibious assault under the specified conditions.
Bombers may attack eligible facilities through strategic bombing; the target and participating bombers must be declared as required.
Tactical bombing may target bases under the rulebook's bombing rules and damage procedures.
Attacking fighters may escort bombers; escorting fighters cannot participate in other battles during that turn.
Defending fighters may intercept bombing raids under the timing and participation restrictions specified by the rules.
Bombers conducting bombing raids are not fired upon by ordinary AAA; the attacked facility provides the applicable antiaircraft cover.
The rulebook defines a special kamikaze-strike procedure for applicable sea zones and powers.
Open Field / Issue: Applicable geographic and political conditions should be kept in the source-specific rule text.

Description: A friendly power may liberate a territory originally controlled by an allied power; ownership and income consequences follow the liberation rules.
Capturing an enemy capital transfers its unspent IPC treasury to the captor and restricts the original controller's purchases and income while it remains captured.
When a capital is liberated, the original controller regains the specified economic and territorial functions, and eligible installations revert according to the rulebook.

Rule: Battle resolution in territories with facilities
Description: Combat units and facilities are handled separately: combat resolves against combat units, while facilities may sustain bombing damage.
Each unit type has a defined purchase cost, attack, defence, movement and special characteristics in its unit profile.
Infantry uses its printed cost, combat values and movement; its attack may be improved by eligible artillery support.
Artillery has its printed profile and may support eligible infantry or mechanized infantry for attack.
Mechanized infantry follows its printed profile and may participate in eligible blitz movement and artillery pairing.
Tanks follow their printed profile and may blitz through qualifying unoccupied hostile territories.
AAA follows its printed movement and special antiaircraft rules; its movement is restricted to the phase specified in the rulebook.
Fighters use their printed profile and follow air movement, landing, carrier, escort and interception rules.
Tactical bombers use their printed profile and follow the air movement, landing, carrier and bombing rules applicable to them.
Strategic bombers use their printed profile and follow the longer-range air movement and strategic bombing rules.
Submarines follow their printed profile and the special rules for surprise strike, submergence, hostile-zone movement and convoy disruption.
Destroyers follow their printed profile and counter specified submarine abilities.
Cruisers follow their printed profile and may conduct offshore bombardment during qualifying amphibious assaults.
Battleships follow their printed profile, take two hits to destroy, can be repaired at a naval base, and may bombard during amphibious assaults.
Carriers follow their printed profile, carry eligible fighters and tactical bombers, take two hits to destroy, and may be repaired at a naval base.
Transports carry land units within their capacity, do not act as surface warships, and follow special loading, unloading and combat-casualty rules.
An eligible unit can pair with only one other unit at a time, though it may pair with different units at different stages of the turn when the rules permit.
Special characteristics listed in the unit profiles modify the general movement or combat rules for those units.
Open Field / Issue: Link individual capabilities to the corresponding rule IDs once the effects schema is finalized.

Description: The rulebook identifies industrial complexes, air bases and naval bases as facilities for applicable rules.
Industrial complexes enable unit mobilization subject to their type, location and operational restrictions.
Minor industrial complexes follow the production and placement limits specified for minor complexes.
Major industrial complexes follow the production and placement limits specified for major complexes.
New industrial complexes may be built only where permitted by the rulebook's ownership, location and production restrictions.
Industrial complexes change control with their territory and are subject to the capital and production rules.
Air bases provide the air-unit range and scramble-related benefits specified in their profile and the relevant rules.
Naval bases increase sea-unit movement from their serviced sea zone and enable applicable capital-ship repairs.
Facilities may receive damage from applicable bombing raids; damage is tracked and can be repaired by spending IPCs.
The operational effects of facility damage and the conditions for using a damaged facility follow the facility-specific rules.
Air bases and naval bases may be targeted by bombing under the rulebook's applicable strategic and tactical bombing procedures.
The supplied number of facility markers is a component count; the rulebook's unit-piece-limit language should be checked separately before generalizing it to facilities.
Open Field / Issue: Do not infer unlimited facility construction solely from the unit-piece rule.

Description: A power controls a territory through the control rules; control determines its territorial income and applicable movement status.
A power takes control of a territory through the applicable combat and control procedure.
Industrial complexes, air bases and naval bases in a captured territory are governed by the territory and capital-capture rules.
The territory's printed power remains its original controller for rules that refer to original ownership, even after control changes.
Liberating an allied territory restores control to its original controller under the liberation rules.
When an enemy capital is captured, the captor takes the original controller's unspent IPCs as specified by the capital rules.
A power whose capital is held by an enemy cannot collect income or purchase new units until the capital is liberated, subject to the exact phase exceptions in the rulebook.
When a capital is liberated, the specified industrial complexes and bases revert to the original controller according to the rulebook.
Control changes update the relevant power's national production marker by the territory's IPC value.
At Collect Income, a power receives the IPC income from territories it controls, subject to capital and other rules.
Eligible enemy sea units may disrupt convoy zones and reduce the affected power's income according to the convoy rules.
Related Data: Sea zones; naval units; convoy zones

Description: Surface warships and submarines can conduct convoy disruption under the applicable sea-zone and political conditions.
Convoy income losses are calculated using the convoy zone's rules and limits; losses cannot exceed the income available under the rule.
Open Field / Issue: Encode exact zone values and caps as parameters rather than duplicating them in generic prose.

Description: Specified powers may receive additional IPC income when the stated control, war-status or other conditions are met.
National-objective eligibility is evaluated at the timing specified by the rulebook, generally during income collection.
Some national objectives award a one-time bonus when their stated condition is first met.
Open Field / Issue: Track one-time eligibility separately from recurring objectives.

Description: The game identifies eleven victory cities whose control is relevant to victory.
The Axis wins by controlling at least eight victory cities continuously for a complete round and controlling an Axis capital at the required check.
The Allies win by controlling Berlin and Rome for a complete round while retaining an Allied capital under the stated condition.
The rulebook's Global Rules section applies when Europe 1940 is combined with Pacific 1940; it is not part of standalone Europe-only play.
In Global play, the United Kingdom maintains separate Europe and Pacific economies for purchases, repairs and income, while its forces operate as a united power.
In Global play, UK units and facilities are mobilized in territories associated with the economy that purchased them.
The Global rulebook defines specific land-territory and sea-zone adjacencies between the Europe and Pacific maps.
Global play uses the combined games' power-specific political and national-objective rules where specified.
The rulebook includes an optional Research & Development rule for the combined game; it is not a standard rule of standalone Europe 1940 play.
When using the optional Global R&D rule, a power marks each developed technology on the Research & Development chart.
The Europe rulebook includes some rules intended only for the combined Global game; inventory entries must retain their scope to avoid applying them to Europe-only play.
